thread:
maria: hey folks, opened a docs PR with migration guidance for rate tiers + a tiny SDK header example. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/512

kevin: quick check 1. Are we renaming the header `X-Usage-Tier` -> `X-Redwood-Tier` globally? need to document fallback behavior.

maria: yes, global rename. i added a note: servers accept either header for 90 days, recommend `X-Redwood-Tier` going forward. included a Python snippet:
```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key)
# per-request override
resp = client.generate("Summarize this.", headers={"X-Redwood-Tier": "pro"})
```

alex: small suggestion: for SDK v2 show using client.headers.update(...) and also include curl example for ops. add mention of `tier_label` in the usage dashboard.

maria: done. pushed a curl example and updated the dashboard link to dashboards/usage-tiers. also added a brief note about how tier labels map to billing tiers.

samira: two things: 1) can we include burst credits math? 2) the docs should show how quotas interact with dedicated customers who have committed capacity.

kevin: yes on both. for burst credits i added this formula in the PR notes: `effective_rate = base_rate + min(burst_credits / window_seconds, burst_cap)` and a short example: base_rate=50rpm, burst_credits=300, window=60 => +5rpm for 60s until credits consumed.

maria: nice. for dedicated customers i'm calling out that reserved capacity bypasses public meter tiers but still uses `tier_label` for analytics. added sample YAML for rollout policy and header usage in private deployments.

docs-bot: reminder: docs PR #512 assigned to @alex for final review. deadline 48h.

alex: will take a look today. leaving earliest comments on the curl snippet and the dashboard anchor IDs. :thumbsup:
